text: A 4-layer board that gives a computer its own phone line: LTE data, SMS and voice calls, with the call audio on USB. Plug in a nano-SIM and one USB-C cable, and the computer can answer a call through your headset, hand it to a script or an AI agent, or send a text. The board was designed by Koppar from a one-page spec ( spec.txt ), then reviewed part by part against the datasheets. One USB-C cable, and the computer sees three ordinary devices through the on-board USB hub: There is no battery, screen or speaker. Three LEDs show NET (green), RING (amber) and CALL (blue). Power is 5 V from USB-C, a 3.8 V / 3 A buck for the module's 2 A transmit bursts, and 3.3 V for the hub, the RP2040 and its flash. The schematic is also in PDF . Board. Upload board/fab/gerbers.zip to JLCPCB: 4 layers, 1.6 mm, stackup JLC04161H-3313 (the antenna feeds are 49 Ω on it). Every via is 0.45 / 0.2 mm and none sits in a pad, so pick Min via hole size 0.2mm/(0.3/0.35mm) and Via covering: Plugged : no via-in-pad, no extra options. Assembly. Use board/fab/jlc/BOM-JLCPCB.csv and CPL-JLCPCB.csv . Glance at the placement preview before confirming, especially the LEDs and the SIM socket (the card slot is at the board edge). REVIEW.md lists the parts the files correct. Parts you source yourself. These are not on JLCPCB's assembly line, or are not on the board at all: Open board/koppar-lte-modem.kicad_pro in KiCad 10. The module's footprint, symbol and 3D model are in the project ( board/footprints , board/custom_syms , board/models ), wired in by the project's library tables. KiCad's library has no 3D model for two of the footprints, so the 3D viewer shows them without a body: easyeda2kicad converts either one to a .wrl you can attach to the footprint. The renders above use them. There is no BOOTSEL button. A blank RP2040 boots into its USB bootloader anyway, and the back has three labelled pad groups for the rest: The modem does not switch itself on: the RP2040 drives its PWRKEY (GPIO22) and RESET_N (GPIO23). Until the firmware runs, the computer sees only the hub and the RP2040. The first version (rev A) had an antenna feed at 35 Ω that hopped layers, a buck 60 mm from its inductor, and a SIM socket facing the wrong way. All three are fixed here, along with the parts list and the assembly rotations. REVIEW.md has every finding with its numbers. VoLTE is optional on the EC25-EUX. Where 2G and 3G are switched off, calls need a module firmware with VoLTE and a carrier that allows it; ask the seller. This board started as a page of text. Koppar takes a spec like spec.txt to a schematic, a routed board, a BOM at live prices and Gerbers. It also takes a KiCad board you already have, or works from your own agent over MCP.
